summary: Junmai Zhang (1886–1969) worked in philosophy and sinology. He studied under Qichao Liang (~1902–1910) and at Waseda (~1906–1910) and Berlin (~1913–1915) universities. He later held posts at Peking University (~1918–1920) and Tsinghua University (~1922–1923).

Junsho Kato is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at KU Leuven and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University, Nagoya University, and Reitaku University, studying under Étienne Lamotte, Hajime Nakamura, and Akira Hirakawa.

Juntarō Ishihama (1888–1968) was a scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and sinological studies. He studied at Kansai University from ~1906 to 1908 and later held posts at Ryukoku University (~1923–1948) and Kansai University (~1948–1963).
Junzo Inagaki is a scholar in Buddhist studies who studied under Shoshin Fukihara. He served as a section chief (課長) at Otani University.

Juri Lotman (1922–1993) worked in linguistics and philosophy. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from 1939 until earning degrees through 1961, and he took up a post at the University of Tartu in 1954.

Shigeaki (Juro) Watanabe is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Gerhard Oberhammer. He held posts at the University of Tsukuba (attested 1989–1990) and as a professor at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2003).
Jushu Nakasone is a Buddhist studies scholar who has held posts as a part-time lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Justin McDaniel is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and later became the Edmund J. and Louise W. Kahn Endowed Professor at the University of Pennsylvania.

Justin Ritzinger specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. After completing his PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett, he held posts at Oberlin College, Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Institute, and Academia Sinica.
Justin Shimeld is a philosopher who earned his PhD at the University of Tasmania, where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.
Justus Günther Grassmann (1779–1852) studied at the Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ~1797 to 1801 and held a post at the Marienstiftsgymnasium from 1806 to 1852.

Justus Olshausen (1800–1882) specialized in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. Educated at Kiel, Berlin, and Paris, he held professorships at Kiel and Königsberg, served as Kurator at Kiel, and later worked in the Prussian ministry.
Jyotirindranath Tagore (1849–1925) was active in linguistics and other fields. He completed his education at the Hindu School and Presidency University (~1864).

János Szerb (1951–1988) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After studying at Eötvös Loránd University (~1975–1980), he held posts at the University of Vienna (1982) and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (1986).

Jérôme Ducor (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Jacques May. He held a post at the University of Lausanne (~1993–2019) and served as treasurer of the International Association of Buddhist Studies (~2002–2011).

Józef Szczepan Kowalewski (1800–1878) specialized in Central Asian, Buddhist, and linguistic studies. After studying at Vilnius and Kazan universities, he served as professor and rector at Kazan State University (1833–1860) and later as professor and dean at the University of Warsaw.
Józef Turczyński (1884–1953) held posts at the Ukrainian National Academy of Music (~1915–1919) and the Chopin University of Music (~1920–1939). His students included Constantin Régamey.

József Budenz (1836–1892) was a linguist who studied at Marburg and Göttingen, where he studied under Theodor Benfey. He worked as a librarian at the Hungarian Academy of Sciences (1861) and as full professor at Eötvös Loránd University (1868–1892).

Jörg B. Quenzer (born 1961) works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He has held an academic post in Japanology at the University of Hamburg (attested 2016, 2026) and served on the editorial board of Studies in Manuscript Cultures (attested 2016).

Jörg Heimbel specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Tibet University and the University of Hamburg under Dorji Wangchuk and Franz-Karl Ehrhard, he has held posts at Hamburg, the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and the University of Munich.
